newsitem.title: GERMANY: German weather stays rainy, barley harvest nears.
newsitem.headline: German weather stays rainy, barley harvest nears.

text.p: Changeable German crop weather with plenty of rain is making up for earlier moisture deficits as farmers prepare for the barley harvest from mid-July, a source at the meteorological office, DWD, said.
Harvests would be delayed by up to ten days because the spring was too cool for crops to develop quickly, and because they needed to dry off, he said.
"But it's not a problem for yields, rather one of rearranging labour schedules," he said.
Only the driest areas in the south of eastern Germany and in northern Bavaria might see some yield losses.
Grains, rapeseed and sugar beet were in good shape, with only maize needing warmer temperatures, DWD said.
Frequent showers were forecast for the next seven days when maximum daytime temperatures should be around 22 degrees.
Continued rainfall might result in lodging, but rain patterns in July/August could not yet be forecast.
The prolonged period of cold temperatures in the spring reduced fungi problems. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
